items.body: Observed: In the past public customer-service conversation, the user wanted a personal everyday-spending credit card, with highest cashback prioritized and no annual fee strongly preferred; work travel was covered by a corporate card. The agent searched the knowledge base multiple times. Retrieved results explicitly supported that the personal Bronze Rewards Card has no annual fee, but did not establish its cashback rate or provide a reliable comparison of personal-card rates and annual fees. Search results included a 3%/1% Green Rewards Card rate, but its article was specifically labeled business, so it does not establish terms for the user's personal-card comparison. The assistant appropriately stated uncertainty and offered human help rather than guessing; the user then reiterated that cashback rates were essential. Inference/limit: available search results in this conversation were insufficient to identify the highest-cashback no-annual-fee personal card. This does not establish that the bank has no such data elsewhere or that no personal-card rates exist. Outcome remains unresolved; no transfer or verified comparison occurred.

items.body:
Observed conversation: A user wanted a personal everyday-spending credit card, saying work travel is covered by a corporate card. Their priorities were the highest cashback possible and avoiding an annual fee unless unavoidable. The assistant searched the knowledge base multiple times. One result documented Bronze Rewards Card as a personal no-annual-fee card, but searches did not yield a confirmed cashback rate for that card or a comparable set of personal-card cashback rates and fees. A result gave Green Rewards Card rates (3% at sustainable/eco-friendly merchants and 1% elsewhere), but it was explicitly labeled as a business card, so it does not establish a suitable personal-card offer. Another general result explained that cash-back-card rewards may appear internally as points and convert at $0.01 per point on statement/checking credit; this does not establish any particular personal card's earning rate. The assistant declined to guess and offered a human agent; no transfer or successful card selection occurred. A later evaluation marker reported success=false, without explaining why.

Ordered procedure for similar inquiry: 1) Clarify that the request concerns personal everyday spending, and record the customer's reward and fee priorities. 2) Search the knowledge base for current personal-card earning rates and annual fees. 3) Verify that each retrieved offer is explicitly for a personal card; do not apply business-card rates to a personal-card recommendation. 4) Compare only cards for which both relevant earning terms and fees are actually supported; account for spending categories only if the customer provides relevant spending patterns. 5) If evidence does not establish the top cashback option or a no-fee alternative, stop short of ranking or recommending a winner, explain what is known (here, Bronze has no annual fee) and what remains unverified (its cashback rate and competitors' personal terms), and offer human assistance without transferring before the customer agrees.

Uncertainty/limits: The observed searches were not proof that no authoritative rate information exists elsewhere or in a different knowledge-base entry. No product terms were verified beyond the cited search results. It is uncertain whether the failed evaluation reflects the incomplete recommendation, the repeated searches, or another criterion; do not infer the cause.

items.body: In a Rho-Bank customer-service interaction, the customer said they had mailed promotional flyers and first asked about a $1,000 statement credit after spending $10,000 in two months. Searches found a similar Business Bronze offer for $500 (and the customer said they were not a business owner), but no confirmation of the customer's $1,000 flyer. The customer then asked about two other flyers: zero foreign transaction fees for three years and a first-year annual fee waiver. Searches found examples of standard 0% foreign transaction fees on some cards, fees on others, and a Platinum card document that mentioned a first-year fee waiver conditionally; none established either flyer-specific promotion or this customer's eligibility. The assistant repeatedly stated it could not confirm or apply the flyer terms and offered human review. After the customer persisted in demanding one of the unavailable offers, the assistant invoked transfer_to_human_agents with reason customer_demands_after_unavailable_offer_refusal. The tool returned “Transfer successful” and said a human agent would assist shortly. Afterward, customer again tried to get the $1,000 credit approved and later directly requested a human; assistant said the existing referral was already in place. Observed outcome: a transfer was reported successful. Unknown: whether an agent actually connected, whether any flyer was genuine or eligible, and whether any offer was honored. The searches and conclusions only reflect the information available in that conversation.

items.body:
Observed: A Rho-Bank customer described three mailed flyer offers: $1,000 statement credit after spending $10,000 in two months; $0 foreign-transaction fees for three years; and first-year annual fee waived. Searches found a similar Business Bronze offer ($500 after $10,000 spend in two months), standard foreign-fee information for some cards, and a reference to what happens when a first-year fee is waived, but did not verify the exact flyer promotions. The customer said they were not a business owner and repeatedly insisted the offers be honored. The assistant explained the mismatch and uncertainty, did not promise or apply any benefit, and asked whether they wanted human review. After repeated insistence, it transferred with reason `customer_demands_after_unavailable_offer_refusal`; the tool reported transfer successful and a human agent would assist shortly. The customer later requested another transfer, and the assistant told them they had already been referred.

Ordered procedure supported by this conversation: (1) Search the knowledge base for the specific flyer terms and relevant card/offer. (2) Compare any result carefully against the flyer; distinguish similar but nonidentical offers and standard card features from the claimed promotion. (3) If the exact offer or eligibility cannot be verified, state that limitation clearly; do not claim the flyer is false, and do not approve/apply the benefit. (4) Offer human-agent review for the unverified flyer. (5) If the customer repeatedly insists on an unavailable/unverified offer after being informed, use the documented `customer_demands_after_unavailable_offer_refusal` transfer reason; verify transfer success from the tool response and tell the customer the referral is underway. (6) If they ask again after successful transfer, explain they have already been referred rather than initiating a duplicate transfer. Stop short of promising approval; final eligibility and whether a human resolves it remain unknown. Uncertain: the conversation provides no confirmed procedure for a one-time initial transfer on the first offer inquiry, and does not establish whether the flyers were genuine or the customer qualified.

items.body:
Observed conversation/tool facts: Wei Chen (user ID 76ad9cc60e) asked why four friends signing up for Rho-Bank credit cards resulted in only two bonuses. Identity was verified and verification logged at 2025-11-14 03:40 EST using account details (the transcript includes email, phone, address, DOB; avoid retaining these sensitive identifiers). Referral lookup returned four records: Bronze Rewards Card COMPLETE dated 10/20/2025; Gold Rewards Card COMPLETE dated 10/22/2025; Silver Rewards Card IN_PROGRESS dated 11/05/2025; Platinum Rewards Card REJECTED dated 10/25/2025. The lookup provided no rejection reason. The assistant said Silver had not yet completed requirements and the rejection reason was not in the record. The customer requested a human investigation of the Platinum rejection; transfer tool returned “Transfer successful” and assistant confirmed a human agent would assist shortly.

Knowledge-base observations: credit-card referral general terms state a maximum of 2 bonuses in a rolling 7-day period, while another credit-card referral document repeats that limit. A general credit-card referral page also lists possible eligibility/active-offer, qualification, and referral-link attribution issues. These are possible explanations only, not established causes in this customer's case. The records do not prove why Platinum was rejected, nor that the weekly cap caused it. Inference/limits: Bronze and Gold are marked COMPLETE, but the transcript does not separately show payout timestamps or independently confirm funds received. Silver is in progress, not confirmed as a final denial. The human transfer was successful; the outcome of the investigation is unknown.

items.body:
Observed in this customer-service conversation: a general credit-card referral article said the limit is up to two successful bonuses in a rolling 7-day window, and that referral status can be checked in the app/online dashboard. The customer supplied email and phone; a user record matched both, and DOB/address were then retrieved from the record. Verification was logged at the tool-provided time (2025-11-14 03:40 EST) before the referral history lookup. The lookup returned four records: Bronze (10/20/2025) COMPLETE, Gold (10/22/2025) COMPLETE, Silver (11/05/2025) IN_PROGRESS, and Platinum (10/25/2025) REJECTED. No rejection reason appeared in the returned Platinum record. The assistant stated the Silver referral may not yet have qualified and that the records did not reveal the Platinum rejection reason. When the customer explicitly requested human investigation, transfer_to_human_agents returned “Transfer successful”; assistant confirmed connection.

Ordered procedure grounded in this observed case: (1) For an account-specific referral question, verify identity using two accepted factors, and log verification before accessing customer records. (2) Retrieve the referral history and inspect each status/date. (3) Report only the statuses and details actually returned; if a rejection reason is absent, say it is not present in the lookup rather than infer a cause. (4) If status is IN_PROGRESS, describe it as unfinished, not as a confirmed failure or payout. (5) When the customer requests human investigation and the available record does not explain the rejection, route to a human agent and verify the transfer result before confirming connection.

Limits/uncertainty: this case established a successful lookup and transfer, not the actual cause of the Platinum rejection or whether the Silver referral later qualified. The general article’s 7-day cap is a possible policy explanation, not evidence that it caused this rejection. The referral history’s dates/statuses alone do not establish link attribution, qualifying spend, offer eligibility, or rejection rationale. This procedure is observed for this Rho-Bank scenario; do not assume other products or cases have identical requirements.

Limits: success was only reported by the user in this instance; no independent validation of the generated link or its continued validity was observed, and offer terms may be time-sensitive.
items.title: Referral-link recovery after missing tool handoff

items.body:
In the conversation, the user first asked for a Crypto-Cash Back card referral link based on a mailed offer claiming $100 after a referred person spent $500 in their first two months. The assistant searched the knowledge base and reported it could not confirm either that card's referral program or those terms; it did not provide a link tool and suggested checking in-app/online banking or contacting support. This establishes only that the available knowledge-base results did not confirm the offer, not whether the letter or offer was valid.

The user then asked about the Business Gold Rewards Card, citing $200 for $7,500 spend within 90 days. A first search returned no matches, but a broader search produced a result documenting a $200 bonus, $7,500 qualifying spend within 90 days, up to 8 yearly bonuses, and acceptance of new referrals only until September 15, 2025. The assistant said the cited terms matched and tried to provide the user tool, but the user reported that it had not actually been given. The assistant then explicitly gave the get_referral_link tool; its response said the tool was now available and required no arguments. The user subsequently reported, “That worked! I've got my referral link now.” Thus the observed outcome is the user's report of successful link generation; no link contents or independent tool execution result were shown in the conversation. This experience does not establish whether the offer remains available after the documented cutoff.
items.title: Referral link request: Crypto-Cash Back unresolved, Business Gold succeeded

items.body:
Observed in the conversation: the user first asked about a Crypto-Cash Back offer ($100 after $500 spend in two months). Knowledge-base search did not confirm that card or those terms; the assistant appropriately said it could not provide a referral tool and suggested checking the app/online banking or calling support. Later, a search result documented a Business Gold Rewards Card referral: $200 after approval and $7,500 spend within 90 days, up to 8 bonuses/year, with new referrals accepted only until 2025-09-15. The user requested a link. The assistant initially only described the referral tool as available, but the user reported it was not actually available. The assistant then invoked the tool-giving action; the tool response confirmed it was given, and the user later reported successful link generation.

Ordered procedure reflected by this experience:
1. Search the knowledge base for the exact card and the claimed referral terms before offering link generation.
2. Compare the customer’s claimed amount and qualification window against the documented offer. If the card/terms are not confirmed, stop: explain the mismatch/uncertainty and suggest authoritative confirmation; do not give a link tool. The Crypto-Cash Back offer remained unverified in this conversation.
3. If a card-specific program and matching terms are documented, confirm the key terms and any acceptance cutoff. For this Business Gold offer, the observed source states $200, $7,500 within 90 days, and a cutoff of 2025-09-15; that cutoff is tied to that source and may not establish present-day availability.
4. Provide the link-generation user tool through the prescribed tool-giving action, rather than merely saying it is available. The actual tool response here showed no arguments were required, despite a knowledge-base instruction elsewhere describing user-supplied user_id and exact card name; this discrepancy makes the correct argument procedure uncertain and should be checked against the live tool interface.
5. Tell the user how to run the tool based on its actual presented interface, then verify availability before claiming it is ready. In this exchange, the user confirmed successful generation, but no tool result containing the generated link itself was observed.

Inference/limits: this experience supports checking exact product-specific terms and explicitly provisioning the discoverable tool; it does not establish that all card referral offers are active, that the 2025 cutoff remains current, or that a referral was successfully attributed or qualified. The knowledge-base instructions and tool-giving response differed on arguments, so do not generalize the no-arguments behavior without checking the actual tool description.

This episode does not establish that a no-argument procedure is generally correct; it conflicts with the internal knowledge-base instruction specifying `user_id` and `card_name`. Preserve this discrepancy and do not generalize beyond this conversation.
